ledger.note: 11 or 10 BC: the Chatti first appear in the record. 'The first clearly recorded event involving the Chatti was the Sugambri attack upon the Chatti in 11 or 10 BC'; they had been Roman allies 'holding land near the Rhine' which they later abandoned to join the Sugambri. The date is that of the first record, not a founding; the land is the page's central Hesse. [Fix pass 2026-10-19: the start stays the first record (conf 1): the Chatti page gives no earlier date.]

ledger.note: 12-9 BC: Drusus's armies overrun the Chatti. Germanic Wars page: '12-9 BC, Invasions of Drusus up the Elbe from the North Sea, the Lippe and Main ... Chatti, Mattiaci, Tencteri and Usipetes are overrun'; the roman-empire dossier holds Germania between the Rhine and the Elbe as an occupation until 9 (its /ledger/20 and /26, counterpart nobody). 'Overrun' is the page's word, not 'occupied': the extent and the continuity of the Roman hold on Hesse are the researcher's reading (confidence 2), and the year is the dossier's first (the page's range begins in 12 BC). [Fix 2026-10-19, reviewer eu-04-x.]

ledger.note: 3rd century: the Chatti fade into the Franks. 'The Chatti apparently continued to exist, and may have become part of the Franks, who were first mentioned in this century'; c. 213 Dio's Caracalla passage names the 'Kenni', which the Valesiana fragment seems to call 'Chattoi'; c. 314 the Laterculus Veronensis lists the 'Cati' between the Bructeri and Burgundians; 392/3 Chatti forces under the Frankish dux Marcomer. No page gives an end; 213 is the last dated trace of a distinct polity and a bridge. [Fix pass 2026-10-19: the Franks page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franks) was opened for the end: it says the Chattuari 'probably all became Frankish' (Laterculus Veronensis, c. 314; attack of 360) and the Frankish name appeared 'around 250', but it does not mention the Chatti or Hessians; 213 stays a conf-1 bridge.]

wars.name: Campaigns of Drusus against the Chatti
wars.outcome: Drusus the Elder campaigned against them in 12-9 BC, 'defeating the Chatti and their Tencteri allies'.
wars.note: No territorial change on the page. [Reviewer eu-04-x, 2026-10-19: war start moved from -12 to -11 to keep the war inside the state's life (first record 11 or 10 BC); the Germanic Wars page has Drusus's invasions in 12-9 BC.]

wars.name: Germanicus's German campaigns (Caecina and Silius against the Chatti)
wars.outcome: Caecina raided their land and burned the capital at Mattium (15); Gaius Silius invaded twice and captured the wife and daughter of the noble Arpus (16); Germanicus celebrated a triumph over 'the Cherusci, Chatti, and Angrivarii' in 17. No territorial change.
wars.note: Germanic Wars page: '14-16: Roman retaliation against Cherusci, Chatti, Bructeri and Marsi'; '17: Cessation of military offensives east of the Rhine'.

wars.name: Chattian-Hermunduri salt war
wars.outcome: The Hermunduri defeated them in a war over a salt-spring river; 'The war was a success for the Hermunduri.'
wars.note: The river is not named on the page.

wars.name: Domitian's Chattian War

zones.text: 'the low basin through the centre of modern Hesse'

wars.outcome: Domitian celebrated a triumph over the Chatti in late 83 or early 84 and fighting continued until 85; in 89 they allied with Saturninus and were attacked by the governor of Germania Inferior.
wars.note: The Germanic Wars page also lists the revolt of Saturninus in 89 'with aid of the Chatti'.

wars.name: Chattian raids on Germania Superior and Raetia
wars.outcome: The Chatti 'attacked southward toward Germania Superior and Raetia and were defeated' in 162; Didius Julianus repulsed them, with the Hermunduri, from the Rhine in 175.
wars.note: No territorial change on the page.

certainty.note: The page gives the Hessian basin, the Eder and the Taunus as limits; no frontier is surveyed.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks (the Chatti are a counterpart of the roman-empire dossier's 14-17 contest, 'Cherusci, Chatti, Bructeri and Marsi', and its 83 gain). Three pages opened. The Chatti page names no kings, gives no area and no infobox. Start is the first record (11 or 10 BC) and the end (213) is a bridge: no page dates the Chatti's absorption into the Franks. The 83 Roman gain in the roman-empire dossier should name 'chatti' instead of 'nobody' once the extent of the annexed ground is found (the Chatti page does not say). Wikidata id unknown. Gazetteer: 'Hameln' and 'Minden' (the Weser towns) are not place names; 'Mattium' and 'Fritzlar' are not either. [Fix pass 2026-10-19: added the 83 loss of the Taunus-Wetterau to Rome (Germanic Wars page) and the Roman occupation of the Chatti land from -11 to 9; the roman-empire dossier's /ledger/20, /26 and /59 should name chatti (and cherusci for 20 and 26). The occupation is the roman-empire dossier's convention: the page says 'overrun', not 'occupied'.] [Fix pass 2026-10-19: the gain from the Cherusci is now around 88 (Chariomerus page), matching cherusci's dissolve.]
